trace.code: attacker supplies an OCSP response (MITM on a stapled/relayed OCSP channel) asserting status GOOD for a revoked/target cert, signed by a throw-away self-signed cert embedded in the response

ngx_http_lua_ffi_ssl_validate_ocsp_response calls OCSP_basic_verify(basic, chain, NULL, OCSP_NOVERIFY): store=NULL + OCSP_NOVERIFY skip ocsp_verify_signer -> the responder cert's chain and OCSP-signing authorization are NOT checked
OCSP_basic_verify verifies only the signature against the embedded (attacker) cert and returns 1; the unauthorized responder is accepted
the Lua caller receives a 'valid' verdict for a certificate whose real OCSP status is revoked -> certificate-revocation bypass

preconditions: an OpenResty/lua-nginx-module app validates OCSP responses via ngx.ocsp.validate_ocsp_response from a source an attacker can influence (MITM on a stapled/relayed OCSP response)
attacker holds/targets a certificate whose real OCSP status is not GOOD

evidence.vulnerable_version: lua-nginx-module with OCSP support, through master @ c686ddb6 (fix 9c61e3da committed 2026-11-28, unreleased; latest tag v0.10.31)
evidence.observed_result: Against the system OpenSSL 3.5.9 (the libcrypto lua-nginx-module links): an OCSP response forged to say GOOD for 'victim.example.com' and signed by an unauthorized self-signed 'attacker-responder' cert is ACCEPTED by the verbatim vulnerable verify (OCSP_basic_verify(basic, chain, NULL, OCSP_NOVERIFY)) and REJECTED by the upstream fix (store={issuer}+PARTIAL_CHAIN, flags 0 -> responder not authorized).

real_exploit.backend: the REAL OpenSSL 3.5.9 OCSP verification stack (same libcrypto lua-nginx-module uses); the verbatim vulnerable vs fixed OCSP_basic_verify calls drive a genuinely forged, attacker-signed OCSP response
real_exploit.demonstrated: a forged GOOD OCSP response signed by an unauthorized self-signed cert is accepted by the vulnerable code (revocation bypass) and rejected by the fix
